BUILDER.AT_LIMIT: You reached the limit of 8 fields. A long form is the main cause of abandonment — to add another one, remove one of those already here.
BUILDER.EMPTY_STEP: This step has no field yet. Add one below or it will not be shown to the visitor.
BUILDER.NO_FIELD_AVAILABLE: Every available field is already in the form. New fields come from the account's custom attributes.

EDITOR.LABEL: Label
EDITOR.LABEL_REQUIRED: The label is what the visitor reads. Without it, the field shows its internal name.
EDITOR.STANDARD_TYPE_LOCKED: Standard field: the type does not change, because it feeds the contact record.
EDITOR.PREVIEW_HINT: Type here to see the mask and the validation as the visitor will. The message only shows when the field loses focus.

VALIDATION.CPF: Check the CPF: the digits do not add up.
VALIDATION.CNPJ: Check the CNPJ: the digits do not add up.
VALIDATION.CPF_CNPJ: Check the document: it is neither a valid CPF nor a valid CNPJ.
VALIDATION.CEP: Check the postal code: it has eight digits.
VALIDATION.CORPORATE_EMAIL: Use your work email, not a free provider.
VALIDATION.PHONE: Enter the phone with the country code, starting with +.
VALIDATION.JUNK_NAME: That name looks incomplete. Is it right?
VALIDATION.JUNK_PHONE: That phone looks like a test number. Is it right?
VALIDATION.JUNK_EMAIL: That email is from a temporary service. Will you get our reply there?

CONDITION.NO_SOURCES: The first step has no earlier field to depend on. A condition only looks at a previous step.
CONDITION.DANGLING: These fields depend on a field that left the form and will never appear: {fields}

MODES.TITLE: How the pre-chat works in this inbox

SIMPLE.LABEL: Simple
SIMPLE.DESCRIPTION: One step, the usual fields. It is what exists today and what most support inboxes need.

BUILDER.LABEL: Builder
BUILDER.DESCRIPTION: Steps, conditions, masks and per-field validation, capped at 8 fields in total.

FLOW.LABEL: Flow
FLOW.DESCRIPTION: The pre-chat becomes the first step of an Automations flow, with the actions and branches from there.

FLOW.EXPLAINER: In this mode the pre-chat is step 1 of a flow: what asks the questions and picks the path is the Automations engine, not this screen.
FLOW.WHERE_TARGET_LIVES: Which flow serves this inbox is not chosen here. The engine resolves it from the flow's own trigger — that is what lets two active flows serve different pages of your site.

MIGRATION.TITLE: Go back to Simple mode?
MIGRATION.DESCRIPTION: No field is deleted: all of them move to step 1. What stops applying are steps {steps} and the conditions on these fields: {fields}.

PREVIEW.EMPTY: No field is on: the visitor goes straight to the conversation.
PREVIEW.STEP_OF: Step {step} of {total} — the next ones show up after this one is answered.

EMPTY_WARNING.TITLE: Any website can embed this widget
EMPTY_WARNING.BODY: While this field is blank, the server sends no frame-protection header, and any page on the internet can load this widget inside an iframe — including a site impersonating yours to collect data from people who believe they are talking to you.
EMPTY_WARNING.ACTION_HINT: To close this, list the domains where the widget should work — one per line. Include all of them: main domain, subdomains, staging, and any other site of the same company. A missing domain stops showing the widget.

SAVE_BAR.PENDING: No pending changes | 1 unsaved change | {count} unsaved changes

UNSAVED_DIALOG.TITLE: Leave without saving?
UNSAVED_DIALOG.DESCRIPTION: These changes were not written yet. If you leave now, they are lost.

CONTRAST.INVALID: Enter a hex color (for example #2DC46F) to see the contrast readout.

EXPLANATION.TEXT: On a light background, {brand} as text gives {ratio}:1 — below the legible minimum. Links and labels will use {adjusted} ({adjustedRatio}:1). The fill stays {brand}.
EXPLANATION.BORDER: As a border and focus ring, {brand} gives {ratio}:1 — below the 3:1 an interface element needs. Borders and focus will use {adjusted} ({adjustedRatio}:1).

OVERRIDE.TITLE: The website overrides this setting
OVERRIDE.BODY: The code installed on the website sets {fields} on its own. What is saved here is the default and the website wins — to make this screen's value count, remove the field from the chatwootSettings object on the site.

THEME.LABEL: Theme mode
THEME.HELP: Automatic follows the visitor's system theme.

AUTO.LABEL: Automatic
AUTO.DESCRIPTION: Follows the system theme of whoever visits the site.

POSITIONS.LEFT_HINT: The bubble sits in the bottom-left corner.
POSITIONS.RIGHT_HINT: The bubble sits in the bottom-right corner.

LAUNCHER.OFFSETS_HINT: In pixels, from 0 to 120. Useful when another element of the site takes the corner.

TYPES.STANDARD_HINT: Just the icon, in a circle.
TYPES.EXPANDED_BUBBLE_HINT: The icon with a call next to it.

LAUNCHER.HIDE_BUBBLE_HINT: Removes the launcher. Only do this if the site opens the chat from its own button — with no launcher and no button, the visitor is left with no way to reach you.

FEATURES.END_CONVERSATION: Let the visitor end the conversation
FEATURES.USE_INBOX_AVATAR_FOR_BOT: Use the inbox name and avatar for the bot

ADVANCED.PANEL_STYLE_HINT: Standard has the header in the brand color; flat uses a neutral background.

SITE_OVERRIDE.TITLE: The snippet on your site can override this
SITE_OVERRIDE.BODY: What you save here is the default, and it now applies to the whole team — it is no longer kept in this browser alone. But if the snippet on your site sets chatwootSettings.position, type, launcherTitle, darkMode, hideMessageBubble or widgetStyle, the site value wins.
SITE_OVERRIDE.ACTION_HINT: If the widget ignores what you saved here, look for chatwootSettings in your site HTML — this screen cannot read your site code.

SUPPORT.LABEL: Support
SUPPORT.DESCRIPTION: For people who already are customers and need help. The widget waits for the click: no invitation, no teaser, CSAT at the end and history over email.

MARKETING.LABEL: Marketing
MARKETING.DESCRIPTION: To turn a visitor into a customer. The widget invites — teaser on a trigger, qualification in the pre-chat and a conversion event at the end.

PROFILE.QUESTION: What is this inbox for?
PROFILE.QUESTION_HELP: Pick now so the inbox is born right. You can change it later, and changing never erases what you configured.
PROFILE.HIDDEN_HINT: The {profile} profile hides these sections — it does not remove them. They stay saved and come back if you switch the profile.

SWITCH_DIALOG.TITLE: Switch this inbox profile
SWITCH_DIALOG.DESCRIPTION: The {profile} profile proposes the changes below. Check what you want applied — anything left unchecked is not touched.
SWITCH_DIALOG.WILL_CHANGE: What changes, if you check it
SWITCH_DIALOG.KEEP_EXPLANATION: Nothing is erased. Every setting of the previous profile stays in the database, inert, and comes back if you switch the profile back.
SWITCH_DIALOG.NOTHING_CHANGES: Nothing changes: this inbox is already set the way the new profile proposes.

PRECHATFORMENABLED.SUPPORT: Turn the pre-chat form off (the customer talks first, no form)
PRECHATFORMENABLED.MARKETING: Turn the pre-chat form on (to qualify the visitor before the conversation)

TRIGGERSPRESET.SUPPORT: Turn triggers off: the widget goes back to waiting for the click
TRIGGERSPRESET.MARKETING: Turn the teaser on with the composite trigger (8 seconds on page AND 30% scroll)

CONTINUITYVIAEMAIL.SUPPORT: Turn email continuity on (history follows into the customer's inbox)

CSATSURVEYENABLED.SUPPORT: Turn the satisfaction survey (CSAT) on when a conversation is resolved

KNOWLEDGEBASE.SUPPORT: Show the Help Center on the widget home screen
KNOWLEDGEBASE.MARKETING: Hide the Help Center on the widget home screen

DISCREET.LABEL: Discreet
DISCREET.DESCRIPTION: A small bubble with one sentence, next to the launcher. No photo.

BOLD.LABEL: Bold
BOLD.DESCRIPTION: A larger bubble, with the photo of whoever answers and shortcuts. This is the default.

AGGRESSIVE.LABEL: Aggressive
AGGRESSIVE.DESCRIPTION: The panel opens by itself, once per session, when the trigger fires.

DEGRADE_ON_RETURN.LABEL: Insist less with visitors already approached
DEGRADE_ON_RETURN.DESCRIPTION: Someone who already saw the approach and did not answer gets the level below on the next visit, then nothing.
DEGRADE_ON_RETURN.SENTENCE: Someone who already got the invitation and did not answer sees a quieter version on the next visit — and after that, only the launcher. This is what keeps the invitation from becoming harassment.
DEGRADE_ON_RETURN.OFF_WARNING: With this off, the same visitor gets the full approach on every visit.

MOBILE.LABEL: On mobile
MOBILE.AGGRESSIVE_NOT_OFFERED: Auto-open is not offered on mobile: the panel covers the whole screen there.
MOBILE.APPLIED_LEVEL: On mobile the applied level is {level} — the panel covers the whole screen, and opening it on its own takes the visitor away from what they were reading.

HOME_INTENTS.LABEL: Intent options on the home screen
HOME_INTENTS.DESCRIPTION: 2 to 4 named options, instead of a "How can I help?". Visitors decide in seconds whether you solve their problem.
HOME_INTENTS.HELP: The text is yours and is shown to the visitor. The identifier stays invisible and lets you compare how each option performs in reports.

SUGGESTIONS.SUPPORT: I need help with an order
SUGGESTIONS.PRODUCT: I want to know the product

ERRORS.NEED_TWO: Keep 2 to 4 options, or none — a single option is not a choice.
ERRORS.DUPLICATED_ID: Two options cannot share the same identifier.

MASTER.LABEL: Enable proactive invitations
MASTER.HINT: While this is off, the widget only shows up when the visitor clicks. Turning it off does not erase what you set here.

RECOMMENDED.LABEL: Recommended
RECOMMENDED.DESCRIPTION: The invitation shows after 8 seconds on the page AND 30% scroll. Both together, and it is what the market study recommends.

ADVANCED.LABEL: Advanced
ADVANCED.DESCRIPTION: Set the seven triggers one by one, with their own value and interval for desktop and mobile.

AUTO_OPEN_DIALOG.TITLE: Open the panel on its own?
AUTO_OPEN_DIALOG.DESCRIPTION: The Aggressive level opens the conversation without the visitor clicking. Three things that will happen:
AUTO_OPEN_DIALOG.POINT_INTERRUPTS: The panel covers part of the page the visitor was reading, and they have to close it to go on.
AUTO_OPEN_DIALOG.POINT_ONCE: It opens at most once per session, and only after the trigger you set — never as soon as the page loads.
AUTO_OPEN_DIALOG.POINT_MOBILE: It is not applied on mobile: there the panel takes the whole screen. Mobile stays on the {level} level.

COMPOSITE_WARNING.TITLE: Time on page alone is not enough
COMPOSITE_WARNING.BODY: With only time turned on, the invitation shows to whoever opened the page and left to get a coffee. Turn scroll on as well: someone who scrolled 30% is actually reading.

TRIGGERS.PUBLIC_WARNING: These rules are visible to anyone who inspects the website's code. Do not use a customer name, a contract value, or any data that cannot be read by any visitor.

TIME_ON_PAGE.LABEL: Time on page
TIME_ON_PAGE.HINT: How many seconds the visitor stays before the invitation.

SCROLL_DEPTH.LABEL: Scroll
SCROLL_DEPTH.HINT: How much of the page the visitor has scrolled.

EXIT_INTENT.LABEL: Exit intent
EXIT_INTENT.HINT: The cursor leaves the page area toward the browser bar. It does not exist on mobile.

IDLE.LABEL: Idle
IDLE.HINT: Seconds with no click, scroll or keystroke.

ELEMENT_CLICK.LABEL: Element click
ELEMENT_CLICK.HINT: The visitor clicks something you pick with a CSS selector.

ELEMENT_VISIBLE.LABEL: Element visible
ELEMENT_VISIBLE.HINT: A part of the page comes into view — the price, the form, the footer.

RETURN_VISIT.LABEL: Returning visitor
RETURN_VISIT.HINT: Someone who has been on the site before.

SELECTOR.LABEL: CSS selector
SELECTOR.SYNTAX_ONLY: We only check how the selector is written — the site is yours, and we have no way to know whether it exists on the page.

FREQUENCY.MAX_PER_SESSION_HINT: At most {max}. Zero turns the invitation off without erasing the setup.
FREQUENCY.COOLDOWN_HINT: In seconds, up to {max} (30 days). It applies to triggers with no interval of their own.

AUDIENCE.URL_HINT: Leave it empty to apply on any page.
AUDIENCE.DEVICE_EMPTY: Pick at least one device — with none, the invitation shows nowhere.

TEASER.EXPLANATION: The campaign is the message; the trigger is the moment. The text below belongs to this inbox's live chat campaign — editing it here edits that campaign, and no new campaign is born because of a trigger.
TEASER.SAVE_ERROR: Could not save the invitation message.
TEASER.EMPTY: This inbox has no live chat campaign yet. Create one under Campaigns to write the invitation text — the trigger decides when it shows, and it stays editable where it always was.
TEASER.SIMULATE: Simulate the trigger in the preview
TEASER.SIMULATE_HINT: Shows the invitation the way the visitor will see it when the trigger fires. Preview only — nothing is sent.

TRACKING.SAVE_ERROR: Could not save the tracking settings.
TRACKING.BLOCKED_BY_502: Storing a credential is not available yet: the encrypted vault is block 5.02, which waits on the cipher keys (0.10). The public identifier above already works and already reaches the site.

META.PIXEL_ID_HINT: It is public: it shows in the code of any site that uses the pixel. Digits only, 15 or 16.
META.PIXEL_ID_INVALID: A Pixel ID has 15 or 16 digits, no letters.
META.TEST_MODE_HINT: Sends events as tests so you can check them in Events Manager without polluting the real numbers. It turns itself off in {days} days.
META.TEST_MODE_EXPIRED: Test mode passed {days} days and turned itself off. Turn it on again if you are still testing.

GOOGLE.MEASUREMENT_ID_HINT: It is public: it starts with G- and shows in the site tag.
GOOGLE.MEASUREMENT_ID_INVALID: A Measurement ID starts with G- followed by letters and numbers.

INSTALL_TAGS.LABEL: Install missing tag
INSTALL_TAGS.HINT: Off by default. When off, we only fire on the Meta/Google tags already present on the page. When on, we install the missing one — always without PageView, so your own page-view count stays untouched.

LEAD_VALUE.TITLE: Lead value
LEAD_VALUE.OFF_HINT: Events go without a value. Use it when the ticket varies too much for an average to mean anything.
LEAD_VALUE.FIXED_HINT: Every lead is worth the same. It is enough for Ads to optimise by conversion.
LEAD_VALUE.BY_RULE_HINT: The value comes from the funnel (block 5.21). Until it exists, the event goes without a value.

ACCOUNT.TITLE: Set for the whole account
ACCOUNT.KILL_WARNING: The account master switch is on: no event leaves any inbox until it is released.

DIAGNOSTICS.PRIVACY: This panel shows the NAMES of the fields sent, never the values — neither in the clear nor hashed. Diagnostics that show a lead's email is a leak with an interface.
DIAGNOSTICS.EMPTY: No delivery recorded yet for this inbox.
DIAGNOSTICS.UNAVAILABLE: Reading the delivery log comes with block 5.14 (audit and diagnostics). Deliveries are already recorded by the server since 5.03 — what is missing is the endpoint that returns them to this screen.

SECRET.SET: Stored. The value is never shown again.
SECRET.SET_AT: Stored on {date}. The value is never shown again.
